sections.h2: Where do I go for property tax questions in Hoke County, NC?
sections.html:
The Hoke County Tax Office has two departments, and both are at 227 N. Main Street in Raeford. The Assessor lists, appraises and assesses all taxable property, and Collections bills and collects tax on real estate, personal property and delinquent motor vehicles.

The mailing address is P.O. Box 1557, Raeford, NC 28376, and the phone is 910-875-8751. The appraisal office is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. According to the county, the roll covers about 28,000 parcels of land, 700 businesses and 40,000 motor vehicles, which is a lot of ground for a county of about 390 square miles of land.

Hoke County was founded in 1911, and Raeford, incorporated in 1901, became the county seat. The county sits between Fayetteville and Cumberland County to the east and Pinehurst and Moore County to the west, and part of Fort Bragg lies on county land.

sections.h2: What rates and fees appear on a Hoke County tax bill?
sections.html:
A bill is built from the county rate, any city rate, a fire district rate and a solid waste fee. The county's tax rates page explains that rates apply to each $100 of value, and that city properties do not get the fire district tax or the solid waste fee.

Rates and fees as printed in the Hoke County tax rates and fees worked examples

Hoke County rate.73 per $100 of value

Fire district rates differ by district, so ask the Tax Office for the sheet that lists the district for your parcel, and confirm the current Raeford rate if the house is inside city limits.

sections.h2: When did Hoke County last revalue property, and what is next?
sections.html:
The last countywide revaluation took effect January 1, 2022. Notices went to all Hoke County taxpayers on February 3, 2022, and the next revaluation is set for January 1, 2030, with work starting two years before.

The county cites G.S. 105-286, which requires reappraisal at least every eight years. Between cycles your assessed value on real property stays tied to the January 1, 2022 market level unless you add improvements or the parcel changes. Ask the assessor how a sale price compares with the 2022 value on your parcel.

The county's description of its appraisal purpose is plain. An appraisal sets each owner's share of the taxes that support schools, roads, parks, public health, libraries, police and fire protection. The amount you pay depends on your property value and the rates adopted each year by elected county and city or town officials.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Hoke County property assessment?
sections.html:
File a Notice of Appeal of Assessment with the Tax Assessor before the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns. The county advertises the adjournment date in the local newspaper and on its website, and the assessor's office can give you the date.

  • Use a separate form for each parcel, signed by the taxpayer or an authorized representative, meaning an attorney or an attorney in fact under a power of attorney if the taxpayer is not a corporation.
  • Bring evidence: appraisals, comparable sales, income and expense statements, or replacement cost.
  • Expect to carry the burden of proof that the value substantially exceeds true market value as of January 1, 2022.
  • Attend the hearing in person or send counsel or an attorney in fact; the board notifies you of the date.

The county's procedures mention informal appeals, and an appraisal already submitted informally does not have to be resubmitted. If you lose at the county board, notice of appeal to the Property Tax Commission is due within 30 days after the board mailed its decision, under G.S. 105-290.

sections.h2: When are Hoke County property taxes due and what happens if I am late?
sections.html:
Taxes are due September 1 under G.S. 105-360 and can be paid at face amount before January 6. After that, interest of 2 percent applies from January 6 to February 1, then three quarters of one percent per month or fraction of a month.

The county lets you pay online, and the Collections office handles questions about bills. Mailed payments count as received on the USPS postmark date, so keep the envelope. A county may also adopt a prepayment discount schedule, so ask whether Hoke County is offering one for the current bill.

Taxes become a lien on the parcel as of the listing date under G.S. 105-355, and the county can enforce the lien through a foreclosure action filed where the land lies. A sale is by public auction at the courthouse door, and anyone redeeming before confirmation pays the taxes plus penalties, interest and costs. Details are in G.S. 105-374.

sections.h2: What tax relief can Hoke County homeowners claim?
sections.html:
The state runs three relief programs, and an owner can use only one. File on Form AV-9 with the county assessor, not the Department of Revenue.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50 percent of appraised value, with a 2026 income limit of $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit on the NCDOR form. Hoke County has 6,926 veterans in the Census count.
  • Circuit breaker: tax limited to 4.0 percent of income up to the limit and 5.0 percent from the limit to 150 percent of it, which is $58,200 for 2026.

The listing period runs the first business day of January through January 31, and the state accepts applications through June 1 before the tax year. A transfer ends the circuit breaker, and the deferred taxes for the three preceding years come due. See NCDOR Form AV-9.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Hoke County housing?
sections.html:
Hoke County is growing quickly. QuickFacts estimates 56,939 residents in July 2025, up 9.3 percent from the April 2020 base, and 22,440 housing units.

  • Median value of owner-occupied housing units, 2020 to 2024: $219,300
  • Owner-occupied rate: 73.0 percent
  • Median gross rent: $1,089
  • Median household income: $64,912
  • Mean travel time to work: 28.8 minutes
  • Building permits in 2025: 558

The population skews young, with 26.7 percent of residents under 18 and 13.1 percent aged 65 or older. The county's economic development page ties growth to Fort Bragg and describes an economy that grew from cotton into poultry, including a turkey processor and an annual North Carolina Fall Festival. The same page notes industrial sites with dual rail service.

sections.h2: What should I do about taxes when selling a Hoke County house?
sections.html:
Ask Collections for a payoff figure for the current year and any prior years before you set a closing date. The tax lien attaches on the listing date, so any unpaid current-year bill has to be settled at closing.

  • Ask the closing attorney to pay taxes from proceeds.
  • Check whether your bill includes a fire district tax and a solid waste fee if the house is outside Raeford.
  • If you plan to claim an exclusion, confirm your filing is current before the sale.
  • Keep the notice of 2022 value for a buyer who asks about the assessment.

faqs.q: Where is the Hoke County Tax Office?
faqs.a: Both the Assessor and Collections are at 227 N. Main Street in Raeford. The mailing address is P.O. Box 1557, Raeford, NC 28376, and the phone is 910-875-8751.

faqs.q: When is the next Hoke County revaluation?
faqs.a: It is scheduled for January 1, 2030. The last one took effect January 1, 2022, with notices mailed February 3, 2022, and work begins two years before the effective date.

faqs.q: What is the Hoke County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county's tax rates page prints a county rate of .73 per $100 in its examples, a Raeford rate of .48 and a North Raeford fire district rate of .10. A solid waste fee can apply outside city limits, so request the current rate sheet.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Hoke County assessment?
faqs.a: File a Notice of Appeal of Assessment for each parcel with the Tax Assessor before the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns, with evidence such as appraisals or comparable sales. The adjournment date is advertised in the newspaper and on the county website.

faqs.q: When do Hoke County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: Taxes are due September 1 and become delinquent after January 5. Interest of 2 percent starts January 6, and later months add three quarters of one percent.
